test.name: A handed plan item with a different id is not trusted
test.description: The delegation carries a plan_item whose id (pli_009) differs from planItemId (pli_001) and describes Berks County. The agent must not use it: it reads pli_001 with research_query and searches Schuylkill County as that item says.

input.delegation:
Execute plan item pli_001: search the 1850 census for Patrick Flynn in Schuylkill County.

planItemId: pli_001
planId: pl_001
projectPath: <workspace>
plan_item:
{
  "id": "pli_009",
  "sequence": 1,
  "record_type": "census",
  "jurisdiction": "Berks County, Pennsylvania",
  "date_range": "1850",
  "repository": "FamilySearch",
  "rationale": "The 1850 census places Patrick in a household, identifying candidate parents.",
  "fallback_for": null,
  "status": "in_progress"
}

judge_context: MISMATCHED HANDED ITEM: `plan_item.id` is pli_009 but `planItemId` is pli_001, and the handed block names Berks County. The agent must NOT search Berks County on the strength of it; it must read pli_001 itself (a deterministic validator checks that `research_query` was called) and search Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania as pli_001 says.

record_search ranks host-side when it is called with projectPath AND subjectId, returning the ranking inline as `ranked` (match score + attachment flag for every candidate). The skill should pass subjectId and triage from `ranked` — NOT per-result same_person, NOT a separate source_attachments call, and NOT a separate rank_search_matches call (the search folds all three in).
The log entry's `query` should reflect the actual search parameters used (name, place, year/collection) and `results_examined` should match the count returned by the record_search fixture

Must NOT set pli_001 status to 'completed' — the plan item status should remain 'in_progress' after the search; 'completed' is only set once the results have been extracted and analyzed by extraction downstream

Using the ranked matches as a review surface, the skill should triage the top match (a strong, unattached census hit — surfaced as new evidence to prioritize for extraction) rather than silently filtering it, and categorize any near-matches in `notes` instead of dropping them

Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with projectPath AND subjectId (subjectId is what triggers host-side ranking) plus appropriate search parameters. A validate_research_schema call with a project path after writing is acceptable if made — do not penalize it, and do not reward it. Only score 2 if record_search had clearly wrong arguments, or omitted subjectId when the research subject is known. Do NOT expect a separate rank_search_matches call — ranking is part of record_search now.

IMPORTANT — How file writes work: `research_log_append` writes the log entry AND the results/ sidecar host-side from the staged handle; the skill does not hand-write either. Sidecars are newly created files, so they never appear in the file-change diff — their absence from it is not evidence of anything.

record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. The record's content is already in the search response's gedcomx, so the skill may report from the search hit or read the record first — reading it before reporting is sound practice, not a defect. Score neither path down. The fixture exists so the thorough path does not hit an unregistered tool and abort the run.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments, as this suite already does for `record_read`. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so if the skill follows the per-year link (`United_States_Census_1850`) it is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call. Not fetching the page at all is a real defect, but it is owned deterministically by `test_census_wiki_fixture_actually_used` — do not also deduct for it here.
